dependency_coverage.name: HighamBench.p12Nearest
dependency_coverage.interpretation: p12Nearest representable exact rounded means that rounded is representable and has absolute distance from exact no greater than that of every representable candidate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The hypothesis makes s a nearest representable value to x+y. Since hx makes x an admissible candidate, it yields |(x+y)-s| ≤ |(x+y)-x|; symmetry and simplification of real absolute value give |s-(x+y)| ≤ |y|.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This is the relational, tie-neutral form of the paper's nearest-addition definition. With representable identified with F, it requires the output to belong to F and minimize distance to the exact sum.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.interpretation: HAdd.hAdd projects the binary operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its explicit instance is instHAdd applied to Real.instAdd, so every occurrence denotes exact addition of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It represents the exact real sum x+y, not the floating-point operation x⊕y.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.interpretation: HSub.hSub projects the binary operation supplied by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its explicit instance is instHSub applied to Real.instSub, so s-(x+y) and the differences inside p12Nearest are exact real differences.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper's error expression uses exact real subtraction between the rounded result and exact sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.interpretation: LE.le projects the binary order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The selected instance is Real.instLE, making the conclusion the ordinary non-strict real inequality.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: Equation (10) is an inclusive ≤ inequality over real absolute values.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real is mathlib's type of mathematical real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The exact operands, rounded result, distances, and bound all live in the real numbers; representability is imposed separately by a predicate.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper treats F as a subset of finite real numbers and evaluates exact reference expressions in R.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real.instAdd supplies the standard real addition operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes x+y the exact mathematical sum used both by p12Nearest and by the error expression.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This matches the unrounded reference quantity x+y in equation (10).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real.instAddGroup supplies the additive-group structure of the reals, including negation and the associated algebraic laws.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the definition of absolute value as max(a,-a) and the standard behavior of real differences.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: These are the ordinary real-algebra semantics used by the paper's absolute-error expression.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real.instLE supplies the standard ordering relation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets nearest-distance comparisons and the final bound using ordinary real ≤.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This matches the order used in the paper's minimum-distance definition and equation (10).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real.instSub defines real subtraction as addition of the negation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All error and distance terms are standard exact real differences.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It matches the signed differences whose magnitudes occur in equations (9) and (10).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Real.lattice supplies max and min operations compatible with the standard real order.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is used by abs to form max(a,-a), hence ordinary real absolute value.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: The paper uses scalar real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.interpretation: abs is defined as max(a,-a) in a lattice-ordered additive group.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real instances, it gives ordinary absolute values for the rounding error and for y.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: This is exactly the scalar magnitude used in |x⊕y-(x+y)| ≤ |y|.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.interpretation: instHAdd converts an Add instance into homogeneous HAdd notation by forwarding hAdd to the instance's add operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instAdd, it resolves every elaborated hAdd occurrence to exact real addition.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It preserves the distinction between the exact sum and the rounded output represented by s.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.interpretation: instHSub converts a Sub instance into homogeneous HSub notation by forwarding hSub to the instance's subtraction operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instSub, it resolves every elaborated hSub occurrence to exact real subtraction.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: It gives the exact difference appearing inside the paper's absolute-error expression.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.interpretation: And is logical conjunction: both component propositions must hold.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Inside p12Nearest it requires both representability of s and global minimality of its distance among representable candidates.
dependency_coverage.paper_match: Both conditions are present in the paper because ⊕ maps into F and returns a nearest member of F.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The verified PDF is the corrected publication of Lange and Oishi, A note on Dekker's FastTwoSum algorithm, Numerische Mathematik 145 (2020), pages 383-403. Equation (9) is on PDF page 5 and equation (10) with its discussion is on PDF page 6.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper quantifies x,y∈F and has a nearest-addition map ⊕:F×F→F, with s=x⊕y.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean quantifies an arbitrary predicate representable and arbitrary reals x,y,s. It assumes representable x, while p12Nearest entails representable s, but it does not assume representable y.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The source binders embed both operands and the result in one floating-point set; Lean strictly broadens the domain by allowing any predicate and a nonrepresentable y.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: For each x,y∈F, a nearest-addition operation selects an output s; tie-breaking is unspecified.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The proposition is universal in s and conditional on p12Nearest representable (x+y) s.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The relational formulation covers every permissible nearest output, including ties, without reversing witness dependence. Any output of the paper's nearest-addition map instantiates s.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper assumes x,y∈F and nearest-addition into the fixed floating-point set F.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean retains representability of x and nearest representability of s but omits representability of y and all structural restrictions on the representable predicate.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: These source hypotheses do not match literally. Their removal is a valid strengthening because the proof of this bound uses only x as a representable comparison candidate.

lean_implies_paper.reasoning: Instantiate representable with membership in the paper's F, take paper operands x,y∈F, and set s=x⊕y. Membership gives hx, while the nearest-addition definition and codomain give p12Nearest F (x+y) s. Lean then yields equation (10) exactly.

paper_implies_lean.reasoning: The paper states the result for its specific floating-point sets, with both operands in F and s produced by a map F×F→F. It does not quantify arbitrary real predicates or cover nonrepresentable y, both of which are included in the Lean proposition.

findings.paper_evidence: The paper assumes x,y∈F for a fixed floating-point system and s=x⊕y∈F.
findings.lean_evidence: The theorem quantifies an arbitrary representability predicate, requires only x and s to be representable, and permits any real y.
findings.impact: This prevents the paper-to-Lean implication but does not lose or distort the benchmark result. The paper statement is a direct, nonvacuous specialization of the Lean theorem.

rationale: The target captures the exact nearest-addition argument behind equations (9) and (10): x is a representable comparison candidate, so a nearest representable s cannot be farther from x+y than x is, and that comparison distance is |y|. All arithmetic and absolute-value dependencies have standard exact-real semantics. Lean strictly strengthens the source by abstracting F to an arbitrary predicate and dropping representability of y; these changes are valid because neither the floating-point structure nor y∈F is needed for this isolated inequality. Consequently Lean implies the paper result, the converse does not hold at the stated generality, and the appropriate accepted classification is faithful-stronger.
